assertions: A versioned managed deployment was registered and remotely verified.
A Process worker launched separate Prefect flow processes and reconstructed the trusted backend through an installed entry-point group.
Only the accepted submission referenced by the dispatched flow was attempted; a second accepted submission remained untouched.
A CSV input was written to PostgreSQL and a second run copied it PostgreSQL-to-PostgreSQL; both replace-mode writes produced an effect record and canonical report.
The managed flows completed, their canonical reports were readable from SQLModel-backed stores, and the PostgreSQL targets contained the expected rows.
The flow-run record was verified against the bound Prefect deployment ID.

runtime.prefect_server: Prefect temporary test server with its own SQLite test database

limitations: Packages were loaded from the uv-managed editable development environment; a clean wheel consumer was not tested.
The submitting process remained alive while the separate Process worker executed.
Only replace-mode CSV-to-PostgreSQL and PostgreSQL-to-PostgreSQL pilots were run; other writer modes were not qualified here.
Prefect's temporary SQLite server emitted a transient database-lock warning while worker readiness loops overlapped; the flow still completed and the test passed.
This smoke did not exercise crash/lost-response recovery, cancellation races, API restart parity, multi-tenant isolation, recurring schedules, least-privilege database grants, or upgrade/rollback.
